title: Earshot: set it up so Claude can read sound
dek: Claude cannot hear. Earshot turns sound into text that Claude can read. This is the setup guide from the SOUND reel, and what we found when we tested it.

blocks.html: Claude reads text and sees pictures. It cannot take in audio. So when Claude edits a video, it cannot hear the sound effects it puts in.

Earshot does not give Claude ears. It turns sound into text: what a sound is, how loud it is and when it starts. Claude reads that text. Earshot also has a bank of 252 sound effects, all made in code, and timing rules measured on professional launch films.
Earshot is free and open source (MIT licence). It runs on your computer, on the CPU. It needs no GPU and no account. This guide uses version 0.4.0, checked on 6 November 2026.

head: Item
Why
rows: Python 3.10 or later
Earshot is a Python program.
ffmpeg and ffprobe
Earshot uses them to read audio and video files. They must be on your PATH.
About 1.1 GB of free disk
Earshot downloads two open models the first time you use it.
Claude Code
Only for step 3. You can use Earshot without it, from the terminal.

items: On a Mac, open Terminal and type brew install ffmpeg. This needs Homebrew.
On Linux, use your package manager, for example sudo apt install ffmpeg.
Type ffmpeg -version. If you see a version number, ffmpeg is installed.
Get the code: git clone https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot && cd earshot
Make a separate Python environment: python3 -m venv .venv
Install PyTorch for the CPU: .venv/bin/python -m pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
Install Earshot with the MCP server: .venv/bin/python -m pip install -e ".[mcp,llm,dev]"
Download the models and test the install: .venv/bin/python -m earshot doctor --load. This step downloads about 1.1 GB. Do it once.
On Windows, use .venv/Scripts/python in place of .venv/bin/python.

blocks.text: Step 3. Connect Earshot to Claude Code

items: Find the full path of your Earshot folder. In that folder, type pwd.
Type this command. Replace /path/to/earshot with that path: claude mcp add earshot --scope user -e EARSHOT_THREADS=3 -- /path/to/earshot/.venv/bin/python -m earshot mcp
Start Claude Code again. Type /mcp. Make sure that earshot is in the list.
Optional: copy the two skills from the skills/ folder of the repo into ~/.claude/skills/. They tell Claude which Earshot command answers which question.

blocks.title: If the first call is slow
blocks.html: Earshot loads its models on the first call. That can take 20 to 40 seconds. In the MCP server the models then stay loaded. On a slow computer, start Claude Code with MCP_TIMEOUT=60000 claude, so the first call does not time out.

In Claude Code, ask in plain words. For example: "Use earshot to make a timeline of reel.mp4 and tell me where each sound effect starts." From the terminal, use the commands below. Put .venv/bin/python -m in front of each one if earshot is not on your PATH.

blocks.title: The commands we used most
head: Command
What it gives you
rows: earshot timeline reel.mp4
A list of the sounds in the file, with the time, the level and a name for each.
earshot critique reel.mp4
A score against 7 professional launch films, with fixes.
earshot sfx list --kind whoosh
The whooshes in the bank of 252, with their ids.
earshot sfx render whoosh_fast/crisp -o w.wav --dur 0.8 --apex 0.32
One sound from the bank, cut to your length, with its loudest point where you want it.
earshot kit init --preset launch -o kit.json
Your own sound kit: one sound for each job (pop, whoosh, hit, tick). Use it again on every reel.
earshot kit render kit.json --out kit
Makes the kit's sound files and measures where each one starts and peaks.

blocks.title: Making new sounds needs your own recordings
blocks.html: earshot forge makes a new sound in code and improves it. To compare against real sounds, it needs reference recordings. Those are licensed and are not in the repo. Without them, forge still runs, but it cannot check the sound against real ones. Start with the bank of 252. It needs no models and no internet.

blocks.text: What we found when we tested it

blocks.html: We tested Earshot on a real reel: 78 seconds, 57 sound effects, all made in code and each tied to a word. Then we made a second version with Earshot's sounds and timing. Same picture, same voice, same music.

head: Test
What happened
rows: Timeline of the finished reel
It named 20 sounds. 9 of them were the voice. It called every section "inspirational corporate background music".
Timeline of the effects alone
It named the pops ("bubble pop") and the thuds ("kick drum"). It did not name the whooshes, the snaps or the ticks.
Version B, with the bank and the launch timing
The effects sat 2 dB clearer over the voice (median). Effects more than 15 dB under the voice went from 18 to 12.
Critique of both versions
Both got 20 of 23, with the same three tips. The score did not see the change.

blocks.title: What Earshot cannot do
blocks.html: It reads a voice-heavy reel badly: it names the voice as sounds and the whole mix as music. Its names for fast effects are often missing. Its score did not change between two versions that measured differently. Use it to pick, time and measure sounds. Do not use it to say whether a reel sounds good. A person must listen to that.

head: Problem
What to do
rows: "ffmpeg not found"
Install ffmpeg (step 1). Then open a new terminal.
The install or the models fail
Type .venv/bin/python -m earshot doctor --load. It says what is missing.
Claude Code does not show earshot
Check the path in the claude mcp add command. It must point to .venv/bin/python inside the Earshot folder.
The first call times out
Start Claude Code with MCP_TIMEOUT=60000 (step 3).
Each terminal command takes 20 to 40 seconds
That is normal: each command loads the models again. For many calls, use the MCP server, where the models stay loaded. sfx, kit and measure load no models.
